approvalRequirements: Be an eligible District of Columbia residential customer at the installation address and select a measure offered under the current DCSEU residential rebate catalog.
Purchase and install equipment that meets the current product, efficiency, installation, contractor, and permit requirements for the selected measure.
Submit the current online or mail rebate application with the dated receipt or paid invoice, model information, installation details, and customer and account information by the applicable deadline.
For HVAC measures, provide the required contractor, installation, and District permit information and allow DCSEU to request additional verification.
Receive DCSEU claim approval while the applicable incentive and program funding remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: DCSEU currently offers rules-based residential rebates for several mapped measures, including qualifying heat pumps, heat-pump water heaters, smart thermostats, refrigerators, and induction or electric cooking equipment. A timely, complete qualifying claim is likely to be approved after administrative review, subject to current funding and measure limits.
reviews.evidenceText: Current DCSEU materials list residential equipment rebates and require measure eligibility, installation, receipts or invoices, measure-specific records, and DCSEU review before payment.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible District of Columbia commercial or multifamily customer with a qualifying project at a DCSEU-served property.
Submit the applicable project information and receive DCSEU preapproval before purchasing equipment or beginning work when required by the current business rebate process.
Install equipment that meets the current measure, efficiency, product, and contractor specifications.
Submit the signed application, current W-9, product specifications, invoices, installation records, and other measure-specific documentation.
Permit post-installation inspection or other verification and receive final DCSEU approval before incentive payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current DCSEU business and multifamily offering uses published measure requirements and project review rather than competitive ranking. A qualifying project that receives any required advance approval and passes final documentation and installation review is likely to receive the approved incentive while funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: DCSEU currently requires business applicants to establish eligibility, obtain required preapproval, and submit tax, product, invoice, and completion documentation for final incentive review.

approvalRequirements: Maintain an active SWEPCO residential electric account for the qualifying single-family residence.
Own or rent the residence and purchase and install a new ENERGY STAR certified Level 2 charging station at that service location.
Complete the installation in accordance with manufacturer instructions, electrical codes, permits, and inspection requirements.
Submit the current rebate request with the receipt, account, charger, and installation information within 30 days after setup.
Allow SWEPCO to verify or inspect the installation and apply while program funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: SWEPCO publishes a fixed residential Level 2 charging-station rebate with objective customer, equipment, timing, and documentation rules. A complete qualifying request is likely to be paid on a first-come basis while funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: SWEPCO currently offers a fixed rebate for a newly installed ENERGY STAR Level 2 charger and requires an active residential account, timely documentation, code-compliant installation, and possible verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Tacoma Power commercial or industrial electric customer at the project site.
Select a current prescriptive or custom efficiency measure and satisfy the applicable equipment, efficiency, installation, and customer-class requirements.

Submit the project application, specifications, proposal, and estimated cost or savings information and obtain Tacoma Power approval before work when the selected pathway requires advance authorization.
Complete the approved project in accordance with the customer agreement and program specifications.
Submit final invoices, equipment records, photographs, and other completion documents and permit inspection or savings verification before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Tacoma Power currently maintains prescriptive and custom business incentive pathways covering lighting, HVAC, controls, refrigeration, envelope, and drive-power work. These pathways are administrative rather than competitively ranked, so a conforming project is likely to receive its approved incentive after required preapproval and final verification.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Tacoma Power business materials provide measure-specific and custom incentives with advance project review where required, signed project terms, and post-installation documentation and verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Tacoma Power residential electric customer or property owner for the installation address.
Choose a currently offered residential measure and satisfy its product, efficiency, building, contractor, permit, and installation requirements.
Complete any measure-specific application, energy assessment, contractor coordination, or advance authorization required before purchase or installation.
Submit the current rebate or incentive request with itemized invoices, receipts, model numbers, permits, photographs, and other required records.
Allow Tacoma Power to inspect or otherwise verify the completed installation before final approval or payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Tacoma Power currently advertises rules-based residential incentives for multiple mapped categories, including heat pumps, thermostats, duct work, insulation, windows, EV charging, lighting, and smart irrigation. A qualifying, documented project is likely to receive the applicable incentive after the measure-specific review process.
reviews.evidenceText: Tacoma Power's current residential incentive hub lists active equipment, weatherization, window, transportation, lighting, and water-saving offers administered through measure-specific applications and verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Tampa Electric business customer and use a measure or service that remains active under the current business efficiency portfolio.

For a variable-frequency-drive or motor-control rebate, install qualifying equipment and provide the account, contractor, specifications, detailed proposal, and paid invoice required by the current offer.
For a custom project or other reviewed pathway, submit project scope, cost, and savings information and obtain any required project authorization.
For an energy audit, schedule and complete the applicable free or paid facility assessment and provide requested facility and usage information.
Do not rely on the former cooling or facility energy-management-system rebate for a new project because those rebate pathways have ended.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Tampa Electric still supports current business audit, variable-frequency-drive, and project-specific efficiency pathways, but the former cooling and facility energy-management-system rebates tied to major mapped categories are closed for new claims. Awardability therefore depends on whether the project fits a remaining active pathway.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Tampa Electric pages keep business audits and variable-frequency-drive incentives available, while stating that the former cooling and facility energy-management rebates ended and their final filing periods have passed.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Tampa Electric residential customer at the installation address.
Select a currently offered heating, cooling, insulation, duct, thermostat, audit, or weatherization measure and meet its equipment and property requirements.
Use a qualified contractor and complete any required energy audit, sizing, permitting, or program coordination for the selected measure.
Submit the applicable rebate documentation, including the paid invoice, equipment and efficiency information, installation records, and permit information when required.
Permit Tampa Electric to inspect or verify the project before final incentive approval.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Tampa Electric currently offers objective residential efficiency pathways for heating and cooling equipment, insulation, ducts, thermostats, audits, and weatherization. A qualifying documented project is likely to be approved, although the legacy mapping to general window replacement is not substantiated as a standalone current rebate.
reviews.evidenceText: Current residential materials describe heating and cooling, insulation, audit, and weatherization services with measure-specific eligibility, contractor, documentation, and verification rules; a standalone window-replacement rebate was not verified.

approvalRequirements: Maintain an active TMLP residential electric account for at least six months and have no past-due account balance.
Purchase and install a new qualifying Level 2 charging station at the residence using a licensed electrician or other qualified professional.
Limit the request to the current household quantity and rebate limits.
Submit the signed rebate agreement and dated purchase and installation documentation for the calendar-year purchase no later than January 31 of the following year.
Receive TMLP application approval while program funding remains available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: TMLP publishes a fixed residential Level 2 charger rebate with objective account, equipment, installer, timing, and documentation rules. A complete qualifying claim is likely to receive a utility bill credit while funding remains; the legacy LED mapping is not part of this EV offer.
reviews.evidenceText: TMLP's current EV program offers a fixed Level 2 charger rebate to qualifying residential accounts after purchase and professional installation, signed documentation, and utility review.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible TMLP residential customer and complete the required no-cost home energy assessment before the heat-pump or weatherization project.

Use a participating heat-pump or weatherization contractor and install equipment that meets the current cold-climate or ground-source qualification rules, including applicable qualified-product-list requirements.
Submit the TMLP Saves application and the required proposal, equipment, customer, audit, and installation documentation.
Obtain advance approval when using the financing pathway; advance approval for the rebate-only pathway may be optional under the current instructions.
Complete post-installation quality assurance and receive final TMLP approval while program funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current TMLP program provides a defined residential rebate path for qualifying air-source and ground-source heat pumps and associated weatherization. Once the audit, contractor, equipment, application, and final quality-assurance requirements are met, the noncompetitive rebate is likely, subject to funding; the legacy LED mapping is unsupported.
reviews.evidenceText: TMLP's 2026 heat-pump offering requires a home energy assessment, eligible contractors and equipment, a program application, and post-installation quality assurance; financing additionally requires advance approval.

approvalRequirements: Maintain an active TMLP residential account for at least six months with no past-due balance.
Purchase a new appliance or control listed in the current rebate chart and install it at the qualifying service address.
Submit the current rebate form with the dated receipt, model and product information, and requested account information within six months of purchase.
Observe the current per-item, household, and percentage-of-purchase-price limits.
Allow TMLP to inspect or verify the product before applying the utility bill credit.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: TMLP currently uses a fixed, documentation-based appliance rebate process for listed products, including qualifying smart thermostats, heat-pump water heaters, room air conditioners, and induction cooking equipment. A compliant listed purchase is likely to receive a bill credit, but the legacy central HVAC, whole-home heat-pump, and LED mappings are not supported by this appliance offer.
reviews.evidenceText: The current appliance program requires an eligible account, a listed product, a dated receipt, timely filing, installation at the account, and utility review or inspection before a bill credit.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible TMLP residential customer and complete the required no-cost home energy assessment.
Use participating contractors and qualifying heat-pump equipment under the current program specifications.
Submit the TMLP Saves application, project proposal, equipment information, and other required program documentation before proceeding with the financing path.
Obtain TMLP project preapproval and separate credit approval from a participating lender before loan commitment.
Complete installation, post-installation quality assurance, and final program approval before financing is finalized or disbursed.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The zero-interest financing path is available for qualifying residential heat-pump work, but approval depends on both TMLP technical review and a participating lender's credit decision, followed by completion verification. Technical eligibility alone does not assure loan approval; the legacy LED mapping is unsupported.
reviews.evidenceText: TMLP currently offers residential heat-pump financing after an energy assessment, eligible contractor and equipment selection, program preapproval, participating-lender approval, and post-installation quality assurance.

approvalRequirements: Be a Washington business engaged in qualifying manufacture, wholesale sale by the manufacturer, or processing for hire of eligible solar energy systems or components.
Report the qualifying activity under the current reduced business-and-occupation tax rate on the applicable excise tax returns.
File the required Annual Tax Performance Report by May 31 following each year in which the incentive is claimed.
Retain manufacturing, sales, payroll, and tax records supporting the reduced rate through the current statutory incentive period.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Washington's current incentive applies to qualifying solar manufacturers and related wholesale or processing activity, not to the purchase or installation of rooftop solar photovoltaic equipment. The mapped building retrofit therefore is unlikely to receive an award from this opportunity.
reviews.evidenceText: Washington currently provides a reduced business-and-occupation tax rate for qualifying solar manufacturing activity and requires tax-return reporting and an annual performance report; it is not a rooftop-installation rebate.

approvalRequirements: No current application or claim pathway exists under the former forest-derived-biomass credit.
Only a legally preserved historical claim for an eligible period before the statutory expiration could remain relevant.
Maintain historical purchase, production, tax-return, and credit records if responding to an audit of a legacy claim.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The Washington credit for forest-derived biomass expired on June 30, 2015. A new biomass or biogas energy retrofit has no current award path under this legacy opportunity; only an unusual preserved historical claim could remain.
reviews.evidenceText: The official Washington code disposition states that the forest-derived-biomass credit expired June 30, 2015, leaving no current credit for a new project.

approvalRequirements: Purchase a qualifying new residential energy storage system for an eligible Colorado residence during the current statutory credit period.
Install and place the system in service and retain the purchase invoice, equipment information, residence information, and vendor certification required to substantiate the credit.
Claim the statutory credit on the Colorado income-tax return or execute Form DR 1307 to assign the credit to the seller or financing party.
When assigning the credit, receive the required purchase-price discount and retain the completed assignment and certification records.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Colorado's residential storage credit is formulaic rather than competitively awarded. A purchaser who installs a qualifying system and completes either the seller-assignment or tax-return documentation should ordinarily receive the statutory benefit, subject to the current credit rules.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Colorado materials provide a residential energy-storage income-tax credit that may be claimed on a return or assigned through DR 1307, with the 2026 law extending the credit period through 2029.

approvalRequirements: Develop a renewable-energy facility that meets Kentucky's current statutory technology, generation-scale, capital-investment, and sale-of-energy requirements.

Submit the prescribed application and project, ownership, financing, permitting, feasibility, investment, and economic-impact information before beginning the disqualifying capital investment or project commitment.
Receive preliminary approval from the Kentucky Economic Development Finance Authority and negotiate the applicable incentive agreement.
Satisfy the conditions for final authority approval and execute the agreement before claiming incentives.
Submit annual eligible-cost, tax, and compliance documentation for any approved refund or incentive claim.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Kentucky's program is a negotiated large-project incentive requiring advance application, authority approvals, and an executed agreement. A large qualifying biomass electric facility may fit, but ordinary solar water heating is outside the electricity-generation scope and eligibility alone does not guarantee authority approval.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Kentucky law requires a qualifying large renewable-energy facility, advance application, authority review, preliminary and final approval, an incentive agreement, and continuing claim documentation.

approvalRequirements: Operate a business that generates or produces electricity within the scope of West Virginia's current business-and-occupation tax statute.
Determine whether the generation activity and energy source satisfy any current statutory exclusion or special tax treatment rather than relying on the legacy program title.
Report taxable and exempt generation correctly on the applicable state tax filings and retain metering, production, sale, and energy-source records.
Do not treat installation of a small rooftop photovoltaic or wind system by itself as an application for a state retrofit award.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current official statute concerns business-and-occupation taxation of electricity generation, not a general rebate or installation award for rooftop solar or small wind systems. The mapped small-building retrofits therefore are unlikely to produce a benefit unless they are part of a qualifying taxed generation business.
reviews.evidenceText: West Virginia's current provision governs business-and-occupation tax treatment for electric-power generation; it does not establish a general application-based incentive for installing rooftop solar or a small wind turbine.

approvalRequirements: Be a Taylor County RECC member with an eligible electrically heated residence or qualifying new manufactured home.
Replace eligible electric-resistance heating with a qualifying high-efficiency air-source heat pump that meets the current minimum efficiency specifications.
Use properly sized and installed equipment and comply with applicable electrical, mechanical, and permitting requirements.
Submit the current rebate request with the account, equipment, model, efficiency, installer, and paid invoice information.
Allow the cooperative to verify the installation and approve the rebate before payment or bill credit.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Taylor County RECC currently publishes a fixed heat-pump rebate for qualifying members who replace specified electric-resistance heating. The process is rules-based, so a properly documented eligible installation is likely to receive the rebate after cooperative verification.
reviews.evidenceText: The cooperative currently offers a heat-pump rebate to eligible electrically heated homes, subject to customer, replacement, efficiency, documentation, and verification requirements.

approvalRequirements: Own an eligible privately held commercial, agricultural, industrial, or qualifying multifamily property located in a Tennessee jurisdiction with an active C-PACER program.
Propose a qualifying energy-efficiency, renewable-energy, water, or resilience improvement, including eligible energy-storage or microgrid work accepted by the local program.
Submit the project, property, ownership, cost, contractor, and technical information required by the program administrator and private capital provider.
Satisfy private-lender underwriting and obtain written consent from every existing mortgage or deed-of-trust holder before closing.
Receive local program approval and execute the financing and special-assessment documents before the C-PACER transaction closes.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Tennessee C-PACER can finance eligible resilience and energy-storage improvements, but approval depends on local program availability, property and project eligibility, private-capital underwriting, mortgage-holder consent, and transaction closing. It is financing rather than an automatic rebate.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Tennessee C-PACER program supports qualifying commercial and multifamily energy and resilience projects through private financing, local eligibility review, lender underwriting, mortgage-holder consent, and a special assessment.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Tucson Electric Power residential customer at the project address.
Select a participating contractor and install a currently qualifying heat pump, air-conditioning or mini-split system, or duct-sealing measure that meets program specifications.
Provide the contractor with the customer, equipment, installation, and project information required for the Efficient Home Program submission.
Permit the program administrator to validate the customer, equipment, contractor, and installation eligibility before approving the incentive.
Complete any requested inspection, correction, or additional documentation before the incentive is issued.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: TEP's Efficient Home Program currently uses participating contractors and published HVAC and duct measure requirements rather than competitive selection. A qualifying installation submitted through the required contractor pathway is likely to receive the incentive after administrative validation.
reviews.evidenceText: TEP currently offers residential incentives for qualifying high-efficiency cooling and heat-pump equipment and duct improvements through participating contractors and program eligibility review.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Tucson Electric Power commercial customer with a qualifying project site.
Work with an approved Trade Ally and submit the application, measure worksheet, specifications, cost information, and required project documentation before beginning work.
Receive written preapproval and incentive reservation before purchasing or installing equipment.
Complete the project to the current technical specifications and retain invoices, equipment records, and installation documentation.
Submit the final application package within 60 days after project completion and permit inspection or other verification before final approval.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: TEP's current business process reserves funds after advance eligibility review and pays qualifying projects after final documentation. Most mapped lighting, HVAC, controls, refrigeration, and energy-management measures are supported, although ordinary low-flow plumbing fixtures and a standalone retro-commissioning study were not clearly verified in the current worksheets.
reviews.evidenceText: The current TEP business process requires a Trade Ally, universal preapproval before work, reserved funds, compliant installation, and a final application with supporting records within 60 days.

approvalRequirements: Be a Texas-New Mexico Power nonresidential distribution customer at the qualifying project site.
Submit the project registration and facility information needed for program enrollment and an energy assessment.
Propose an eligible prescriptive or custom efficiency measure and provide the equipment, baseline, cost, operating, and expected-savings information requested by the program.
Complete the approved installation and submit final invoices, equipment records, and project-completion documentation.
Permit TNMP or its implementer to validate installation and annual demand and energy savings before calculating and paying the incentive.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: TNMP currently offers cash incentives based on validated energy and demand savings for eligible nonresidential projects. Lighting, HVAC, envelope, motors, drives, and custom work have a defined path, so a reviewed and verified project is likely to receive the calculated incentive; refrigeration, dishwashing, and building-automation mappings may require custom acceptance.
reviews.evidenceText: TNMP's current large-commercial program enrolls nonresidential customers, assesses projects, and pays savings-based incentives after project registration, installation documentation, and validated demand and energy savings.

approvalRequirements: Serve an eligible Texas-New Mexico Power residential customer through a project sponsor accepted into the current Residential or Hard-to-Reach Standard Offer Program.
Confirm program budget, site, customer, and measure eligibility and execute the required Host Customer Agreement before work begins.
Do not remove baseline equipment or install measures before the sponsor's program agreement and project authorization are in place.
Install measures that meet the current technical, equipment, contractor, and customer-qualification rules, including linked solar requirements where storage or EV charging depends on them.
Submit measure, customer, invoice, installation, and savings documentation and permit inspection or verification before TNMP pays the project sponsor.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: TNMP's 2026 program uses accepted project sponsors, advance customer agreements, published measure rules, and post-installation verification. Qualifying projects are generally paid under the standard-offer structure rather than competitively ranked, although the incentive is paid to the sponsor and battery or EV charging measures have linked solar conditions.
reviews.evidenceText: The current TNMP manual requires an accepted sponsor, budget confirmation, a signed customer agreement before work, compliant installation, documentation, and inspection before sponsor payment; current measures include HVAC, envelope, controls, water, solar, storage, and EV charging under specified conditions.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible electric member of The Energy Cooperative at the installation address.
Purchase and install a measure listed in the current rebate program and meet its ENERGY STAR, efficiency, equipment, and installation requirements.
Submit the applicable rebate application with the paid invoice or receipt, model and serial information, photographs, and other measure-specific records.
Observe the current household and annual rebate quantity limits.
Permit the cooperative to conduct the required visual inspection before applying the rebate as a utility bill credit.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The Energy Cooperative currently publishes fixed rebates for qualifying heat pumps, geothermal systems, refrigerators, and Level 2 chargers. These are rules-based member incentives, so a complete eligible claim is likely to receive the bill credit after required inspection and documentation review.
reviews.evidenceText: Current cooperative materials limit rebates to electric members, list fixed qualifying equipment incentives, require supporting purchase and installation records, and use visual inspection and bill-credit payment.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Pennsylvania commercial, nonprofit, community-serving, or multifamily borrower with a qualifying building project.
Propose a capital energy project capable of meeting the program's required energy-performance target; on-site renewable energy must be part of a larger efficiency project.
Submit an initial financing request with ownership, project scope, energy analysis, costs, sources and uses, contractor, schedule, and organizational and financial information.
Pass program-fit review, energy and technical review, borrower credit underwriting, collateral evaluation, and any guarantee requirements.
Complete the required pre-closing affidavits and loan documents and satisfy post-project measurement and verification obligations.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: GELF is underwritten project financing, not an entitlement. A qualifying retrofit can be financed only after energy-performance, borrower, collateral, and transaction review. A standalone energy audit does not itself meet the stated energy-reduction objective, while retro-commissioning may fit only when it produces or supports a qualifying capital project.
reviews.evidenceText: Current GELF materials require an eligible Pennsylvania building project with substantial energy reduction, followed by project-fit, technical, credit, collateral, closing, and measurement-and-verification review.

approvalRequirements: Be a Tideland EMC member with service in the member's name and qualifying property ownership for at least 12 months.
Complete Tideland EMC's free energy audit before beginning the financed weatherization or HVAC work.
Select an eligible measure and submit the contractor proposal and required technical records, including a heat-gain and heat-loss calculation for HVAC work.
Pass the cooperative's credit review, payment-history and ability-to-repay standards, bankruptcy restriction, and any deed-of-trust requirement for a larger loan.
After approval, complete the project within 90 days, provide final documentation, and satisfy any inspection or funding conditions.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current program offers defined low-interest financing for eligible HVAC and weatherization work, but approval depends on the energy audit, creditworthiness, account and title history, project review, security, funding, and timely completion. Battery storage is not expressly listed and would require separate confirmation as an eligible coordinated demand-reducing device.
reviews.evidenceText: Tideland EMC currently requires a pre-project energy audit, eligible work, contractor and technical documentation, credit underwriting, possible collateral, available funds, and completion within 90 days after approval.
